title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 59
paragraphs: Doriscus is a seashore and a plain of great size in Thrace, through which the great river Hebrus flows. Here a royal fortress had been built — the one now called Doriscus — and a Persian garrison had been stationed in it by Darius, ever since the time when he went on his march against the Scythians. The place seemed to Xerxes convenient for marshaling and counting his army, and he proceeded to do so. The commanders of the ships, at Xerxes's bidding, had brought all the vessels, when they reached Doriscus, up to the shore adjoining it, on which stand the Samothracian city of Sale and also Zone, whose furthest point is the promontory of Serreion, a well-known landmark. This region in ancient times had belonged to the Cicones. The ships were beached there, and while they lay drawn up and drying out, he was numbering the army at Doriscus.
